gaussians_to_voxel — 3D transform op

• Data kinds: points → voxel

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.gaussians_to_voxel(means, scales, opacities, size, bounds, device='cpu') (to call the implementation directly, import match3d; match3d.gaussians_to_voxel(means, scales, opacities, size, bounds, device='cpu'); from the registry, ops3d.get("gaussians_to_voxel"))

• GPU: this op has a GPU path (device="cuda")

Usage

3DGS (anisotropic Gaussians) → a density voxel volume. Each Gaussian is placed at its mean with its opacity, then smoothed by the mean scale.

Approximation (isotropic splat + smoothing): exact anisotropic covariance rasterisation is heavy, so the means are first splatted with opacity weights → gaussian smoothing by the mean scale. Sufficient for coarse alignment in matching.

Arguments: means (N,3) centres; opacities is reshaped to length N and becomes the splat weight (opacity is added where points_to_voxel adds 1). scales of any shape is reduced to 1 single mean value, and σ = mean(scales)/mean(hi − lo)·size (world length → voxel length) is used as the smoothing width (lower bound 0.5 voxel; σ=1 if scales is empty). Anisotropy and rotation are ignored. bounds=(lo, hi) is required (None not allowed; validated by _lo_hi, ValueError if invalid). Out-of-range centres are clipped to the edge voxel. Returns (size, size, size) float64; axis order = column order of means. The opacity sum is roughly preserved but not normalised. To get a point cloud instead, use gaussians_to_points.
